featureRequest:
# Regroup top-bar controls (and 5 more)

This request comes from a conversation with the developer about their app.
Anything marked suspected or not checked is a guess: confirm it in the code before building on it.

## What this is about
Tinkerdeck's screen overwhelms novices: about 10 ungrouped top-bar controls, six stacked parts per app and up to five banners all show at once, and the features look added one release at a time. The developer wants a tidy-up, not a redesign: regroup controls, hide parts that are not in use (at start and on demand), remember the layout between sessions, add VS Code-style shortcuts and a command palette. Maintained npm packages should be preferred over hand-built components.

## What to build or fix

### 1. Regroup top-bar controls (confirmed)
The top bar has about 10 ungrouped controls: sidebar toggle, logo, name, global Shell dropdown, Editor, Updates, Refresh, Help, theme picker, light/dark toggle and + App. Group related ones, for example shell, theme, updates and help in one Settings menu. Keep sidebar toggle, name and + App visible. The exact list of what counts as advanced is not settled and is to be decided in the plan. Keep the current structure; the editor stays a separate full view.

Evidence:
- src/App.tsx:300-363

### 2. Hide unused parts at start and on demand (confirmed)
An app view stacks AppHeader, GitBar, TabStrip, terminals, ConsoleNav and GitDrawer, and git has two entry points (GitBar and GitDrawer). Up to five banners (lock, job warning, update, manual-update result, error) can show at once, plus about 8 dialogs. Start with optional parts hidden or collapsed. Suggestions (not verified on screen): show GitBar only when the folder is a git repo and the user opens it, or collapse it to a branch chip; collapse ConsoleNav when there is one console; merge update and manual-update banners into one notification spot while keeping lock, job warning and error visible; lazy-load git parts and dialogs with React.lazy/Suspense. Also make open parts hideable, with a 'Reset layout' action that returns to the calm default view. Reset must hide running consoles, not close them, because closing a running terminal asks for confirmation today.

Evidence:
- src/App.tsx:451-531
- src/App.tsx:365-405
- src/App.tsx:549-676
- src/App.tsx:61
- src/App.tsx:62-65
- src/features/editor/EditorView.tsx:12-14

### 3. Remember layout between sessions (confirmed)
Persist the open/hidden state of the optional parts and restore it on the next start. Today only the sidebar collapsed state (paneCollapsed) is read from saved settings. gitTab, help, update and finder flags are not shown to be saved. Whether every part has a hide control today has not been checked.

Evidence:
- src/App.tsx:62-65
- src/App.tsx:69

### 4. VS Code-style keyboard shortcuts (confirmed)
Add shortcuts modelled on VS Code, for example Ctrl+Shift+P palette, Ctrl+` console, Ctrl+Shift+G git, Ctrl+P or Ctrl+O to open the editor. Only Ctrl+B and F5 exist at app level now. The terminal passes only those through, so every new shortcut must be added to the terminal's pass-through list or the terminal will swallow it. The editor has its own Ctrl+S and Ctrl+N, which must not clash.

Evidence:
- src/App.tsx:120-134
- src/features/terminals/TerminalHost.tsx:75-77
- src/features/editor/EditorView.tsx:28

### 5. Command palette (confirmed)
Add a command palette (Ctrl+Shift+P) that lists every action with its shortcut, so hidden controls stay findable. Include a 'Reset layout' action and actions for toggling each optional part.

Evidence:
- src/App.tsx:120-134 (no palette or action registry exists today)

### 6. Use maintained npm packages for components (not checked)
Prefer reliable, free, well-supported packages over hand-built components. Candidates (suggestions, not yet verified): cmdk for the palette, react-hotkeys-hook for shortcuts (replacing the hand-written handler), Radix dropdown-menu and dialog for menus and dialogs, react-resizable-panels for panes, React.lazy for lazy loading. Before committing to any package, the plan must check it works with React 18.3 and the Tauri webview, its license and maintenance, and how it fits the app's themes and CSS. None of these is installed today. React 18, framer-motion, marked, dompurify, CodeMirror and xterm are already used.

Evidence:
- package.json (react ^18.3.1, framer-motion; no cmdk, radix or hotkeys packages)
- src/App.tsx:120-134

## Not part of this
- Redesigning the views or their structure
- Moving the editor into the app view; it stays a separate full view
- Log or terminal output noise (the developer meant UI clutter)

## Not settled yet (do not treat as fact)
- Which controls count as advanced and get hidden, and which the developer uses daily?
- Which banners and git entry points stay visible?
- Do all optional parts already have a hide control? Only the state declarations were read.
- Do the candidate packages work with React 18.3, the Tauri webview and the app's styling?
- The CSS and the real on-screen look were not inspected.

## Requirements agreed in the conversation

The developer and the assistant already agreed these while talking. Build on them; do not ask again what they settle.

- **R1**: Inspect the current Tinkerdeck interface and write a tidy-up plan that, for each screen, panel, dialog, footer element, top-bar control and keyboard shortcut, states where it lives afterwards: the named group it belongs to, whether it is shown by default or hidden until needed (by collapsing into a pane or by lazy loading), how it is hidden again once it is open, whether its open/collapsed/hidden state is remembered between sessions, and where any hidden item and each shortcut is reached from.
  - Done when: The plan names every current screen, panel, dialog, footer element, top-bar control and shortcut and states where each one lives after the tidy-up.
  - Done when: The plan states, for each optional part, how it is hidden again after being opened and whether its open/hidden state is saved between sessions.
  - Done when: A reviewer can trace any current function to exactly one place in the plan.
  - Done when: The plan is checked against the running app, not only against src/App.tsx, before it is agreed, including which parts already load lazily and which are always on screen.
  - Done when: The plan says, for each new UI building block it introduces, whether a maintained npm package is used or it is built in-house, and why.
- **R2**: Keep the current screens, panels, dialogs, the footer and the separate editor view; the tidy-up changes only how controls are grouped, which are shown by default or hidden until needed, how open parts can be hidden again, which state is remembered and which shortcuts exist, without redesigning views or embedding the editor inside the app view.
  - Done when: The plan changes only control grouping, default visibility (collapsing or lazy loading), on-demand hiding, remembered layout and shortcuts; it does not redesign or replace existing screens, panels, dialogs or the footer.
  - Done when: The editor remains a separate view rather than being folded into the app view.
  - Done when: The footer stays visible, including after open parts are hidden.
- **R3**: Group related controls into named groups with a stated purpose, keep Shell and Theme directly reachable instead of moving them behind a dialog, and hide advanced or rarely used controls so a first-time user sees fewer controls, while the primary actions (open an app, run a command, open Git, toggle the sidebar) stay visible without opening any hidden area.
  - Done when: A first-time user can point to where opening an app, running a command, opening Git and toggling the sidebar live without opening a hidden or secondary area.
  - Done when: Shell and Theme can be reached without opening a dialog.
  - Done when: Every hidden control is reachable from one clearly named place, and nothing becomes unreachable.
  - Done when: The plan lists each control and whether it is visible by default or hidden as advanced.
- **R4**: Add VS Code-style keyboard shortcuts while keeping the existing app shortcuts: Ctrl+B toggles the sidebar, F5 refreshes, Ctrl+Shift+P opens a command palette, and a shortcut switches the theme.
  - Done when: Ctrl+B toggles the sidebar, F5 refreshes, Ctrl+Shift+P opens the command palette, and the theme shortcut switches the theme.
  - Done when: The app-level shortcuts still work when focus is inside the app view, including when the terminal is focused.
  - Done when: The plan lists every shortcut and what it does, and the command palette lists the actions it can run together with their shortcuts.
- **R5**: Hide parts the user is not working on instead of keeping them on screen: collapse or lazy-load the git tools and the console until they are used, and lazy-load dialogs and tool panels that are not shown, while keeping the git drawer's existing hidden-until-opened behaviour.
  - Done when: Opening an app that has a git repo and a console does not show the git tools or the console until the user asks for them.
  - Done when: A collapsed or lazy-loaded part is reachable when needed, and nothing becomes unreachable.
  - Done when: The parts that are not shown are loaded when needed rather than up front, so the initial view does not carry them.
  - Done when: The git drawer stays hidden until opened, as it does today.
- **R6**: Keep the footer, and make its toggle behave the same as the sidebar's Ctrl+B toggle so the two stay in step.
  - Done when: Clicking the footer toggle and pressing Ctrl+B produce the same result.
  - Done when: The footer remains visible.
- **R7**: Add a command palette that lists every action with its name and its shortcut, so that any control hidden from the default view can still be found and run by typing its name.
  - Done when: The command palette lists every action the app offers, each with the shortcut that runs it, or a clear note that it has none.
  - Done when: Typing the name of a hidden control in the command palette finds that control and runs it.
  - Done when: The command palette opens with Ctrl+Shift+P even when the terminal or editor is focused.
  - Done when: A query that matches no action shows an empty result.
- **R8**: Any optional part the user has opened (the git drawer, the console, extra panes, dialogs and banners) can be hidden again on demand, so after prolonged use the user can return to a calm default view without restarting the app, and hiding an open console does not close the terminal or lose its output.
  - Done when: Every optional part that can be opened also has a control that hides it again.
  - Done when: After hiding the open optional parts, the screen shows the default minimal view with the primary actions and the footer still visible.
  - Done when: A hidden part can be reopened from the same named place, and via the command palette, as when it was first closed.
  - Done when: Hiding an open console keeps the terminal running and its output available, rather than closing it.
- **R9**: Remember the last layout between sessions: for each optional part, whether it is open, collapsed or hidden is saved when the app closes and restored when it reopens, so the user does not have to rearrange the screen each time.
  - Done when: Reopening the app restores the previous session's open, collapsed or hidden state for the optional parts the plan covers (sidebar, git drawer, console, panes and dialogs).
  - Done when: A part the user hid stays hidden in the next session; a part the user left open reopens open.
  - Done when: On first run, or when no saved layout exists, the app starts in the default minimal view.
  - Done when: A saved layout that can no longer be applied falls back to the default for the affected part instead of failing.
- **R10**: Build the new UI building blocks from reliable, free, safe and well-supported npm packages instead of hand-rolling them: the command palette, shortcut handling, menus, dialogs and resizable or collapsible panes each use an established package where a suitable one exists, and anything built in-house is a stated choice with a reason.
  - Done when: For each building block (command palette, keyboard shortcuts, menus, dialogs, resizable or collapsible panes), the plan names the package used or states that it is built in-house with the reason.
  - Done when: Each chosen package is free to use, openly licensed, actively maintained, and confirmed to work with React 18.3 inside the Tauri webview before the plan commits to it.
  - Done when: The chosen packages do not change what the existing controls do, and every existing shortcut still works as R4 requires.
  - Done when: Where the app already has a suitable library installed (for example framer-motion, CodeMirror, xterm), the plan says whether it is reused before adding another.

Not part of this: Implementing the tidy-up in code before the plan is agreed.; Redesigning screens, views or navigation flow, or embedding the editor inside the app view.; Changing what existing functions do; the plan changes where they live, how they are grouped, whether they show by default, whether they are remembered and which shortcuts reach them.; Moving the Shell or Theme controls behind a dialog.; Backend, data-storage or permission changes.

<!--devteam-requirements:-->

sliceReports.summary: Built the slice-1 parts of the R1-R5 tidy-up: (1) docs/ui-tidy-up-plan.md, the R1 inventory that names every screen, panel, dialog, banner, the eleven top-bar controls and every shortcut, with its named group, default visibility, how it is hidden again, remembered state and entry point, plus the lazy/eager record, package decisions, R1 edge cases, gaps and the A2 per-screen running-app checklist; (2) src/features/apps/TopBar.tsx + TopBar.module.css, extracting the header into four named groups (Brand, Appearance, Create, Utilities) with Shell, Theme and the primary actions always visible and wrapping instead of clipping; (3) src/features/apps/UtilitiesMenu.tsx + UtilitiesMenu.module.css, one menu holding the advanced Editor, Updates, Refresh and Help commands, hidden until opened and hidden again on choose, Escape or click-outside, with an update-available badge so a waiting update stays noticeable; (4) src/features/apps/AppFooter.tsx + AppFooter.module.css, the slim persistent role=contentinfo status strip showing the app version only; (5) src/App.tsx now renders TopBar and AppFooter and code-splits EditPane, GitDrawer, ConsoleNav and the ThemeFinder body under Suspense, and src/App.module.css drops the moved header rules and adds the lazy fallbacks. Existing App tests were adapted where a control moved into the Utilities menu or a panel became lazy. Shortcut registry, command palette, Git branch-chip collapse and the terminal pass-through belong to the other slices of this build and were not touched. Verified with npm run lint, npm test (37 files, 364 tests pass) and npm run build.

sliceReports.summary: Slice 2 of 4. Added src/shared/shortcuts.ts: one registry plus matchShortcut/isAppShortcut for Ctrl+B (sidebar), F5 (refresh), Ctrl+Shift+P (palette) and Ctrl+Alt+T (theme), deliberately not matching the editor's Ctrl+S/N/O/W. TerminalHost now uses the shared predicate in attachCustomKeyEventHandler, so the four app shortcuts reach the window while the focused terminal keeps Ctrl+C/Ctrl+V and every other key. Tests: shortcuts registry, palette, git chip collapse and terminal pass-through. Also reported here are the run's existing tests that cover R1-R3 (plan, footer, grouped top bar/Utilities) so every revision-1 requirement ID appears in the report.

lastPlanConflicts.why: R3 regroups the top-bar controls into named groups, and the design does this by hand-building TopBar, UtilitiesMenu, AppFooter and a command palette, explicitly leaving the jattac packages installed 'in preference of any other components' for a later revision; a UtilitiesMenu performs the same function as jattac.libs.web.overflow-menu and the new buttons the same function as zest-button.
lastPlanConflicts.evidence: USR-001 (blocking): 'use the following npm i jattac.libs.web.zest-responsive-layout, ... npm i jattac.libs.web.overflow-menu, and npm i jattac-web-poller in preference of any other components or native ui elements that may perform the same function'. Design: 'a small in-house command palette'; 'No npm package is added in this revision ... jattac overflow-menu/zest-button, cmdk, react-hotkeys-hook and Radix remain candidates for revision 2's R10 package verification against React 18.3 and the Tauri webview.'

lastPlanConflicts.why: R5 requires dialogs that are not shown to be lazy-loaded so the initial view does not carry them; the design keeps UpdateDialog in the eager module purely because it shares a file with the always-needed banner, which is a co-location convenience, not a technical necessity (the module can be split).
lastPlanConflicts.evidence: R5: 'lazy-load dialogs and tool panels that are not shown' and 'Do not load the git tools, console or dialogs as part of the initial view.' Design: 'UpdateDialog stays with UpdateBanner because the always-needed banner and the dialog live in one module today.'

lastPlanConflicts.why: The design's scope and impact include src/App.module.css, which is an old area, and it says the header rules are moved out of it. No requirement needs the existing header rules removed: the new TopBar.module.css can carry the new rules while the old file is left alone, so this is a reorganisation of an old file for convenience. The design states no technical reason why new code plus an adapter in features/ cannot meet R3 without touching the old stylesheet.

Design: component 'TidyUpPlan', path 'docs/ui-tidy-up-plan.md', requirements ['R1','A2']; A2 acceptance 'The developer signs the checklist off before the UI change is merged.' No test component (TopBar, UtilitiesMenu, AppFooter, Shortcuts, CommandPalette, GitBar.collapse, TerminalHost.shortcuts, App.shortcuts) lists R1.

conflicts.why: R2 says the tidy-up keeps the current footer and 'changes only' control grouping, default visibility, on-demand hiding, remembered layout and shortcuts, but no footer exists in the app today; the design therefore adds a brand-new footer strip, which is a new UI element outside those allowed changes. R2's two halves (keep the footer / change only those things) cannot both hold, so the requirement must say which wins.
conflicts.evidence: R2: 'Keep every current screen, panel, dialog, the footer and the separate editor view; the tidy-up changes only how controls are grouped, which are shown by default or hidden until needed, how open parts can be hidden again, which state is remembered and which shortcuts exist.' Design: 'Because R2/R6 name a footer but none exists today, a slim persistent footer strip is added showing the app version.' Analyst fact: 'no footer element exists anywhere in src or index.html.'

planRounds.resolution: You chose: Keep the requirement, and relax USR-001, TEST-001 for this feature

findings.description: R5 requires dialogs that are not shown to be lazy-loaded, and its pitfall says 'Do not load the git tools, console or dialogs as part of the initial view'. Here only one dialog body (ThemeFinder) plus the palette are split; the other eight modal dialogs remain in the initial bundle. Move the dialog bodies (at least Help, UpdateDialog and the big texts) into lazy modules rendered under Suspense so the initial view does not carry them.
findings.evidence: Only ConsoleNav, EditPane, GitDrawer, ThemeFinder and CommandPalette are React.lazy (src/App.tsx:41-45). Every modal dialog is still inline in the eagerly loaded App module: Stop running terminals? (551-570), Delete <app>? (572-583), Close <console>? (585-604), Switch to <branch>? (606-625), Start the apps that were running last time? (627-640), Quit Tinkerdeck? (642-652), Update to <version> (654-669, UpdateDialog comes from the eagerly imported UpdateUI at line 16) and Help (671-702). A Vite build of this tree (outDir sent to scratch) puts 'Stop running terminals', 'Delete ', 'Quit Tinkerdeck', 'Start the apps that were running last time', 'Switch to', 'Update to', 'Find themes' and the Help text into the initial index-*.js chunk, while lazily split strings such as 'Search commands' and 'Close git panel' appear only in separate chunks. The plan even claims 'Initial view therefore carries none of ... the dialogs' bodies' (docs/ui-tidy-up-plan.md:168-170), which is false.
findings.note: confirmed by the whole Challenge after being built (The modal dialog bodies are now lazy modules rendered under Suspense: ConfirmDialogs (src/App.tsx:52, used at 567), HelpDialog (src/App.tsx:49, used at 666) and UpdateDialog (src/App.tsx:48, used at 647) join UpdateBanner (47) next to the existing lazy panels (40-44). ConfirmDialogs and HelpDialog are exported from src/features/command-palette/CommandPalette.tsx (lines 106 and 205), so their bodies share the palette's on-demand chunk. I rebuilt the tree with `npx vite build` (outDir in scratch/reviewer/dist-r6) and searched the entry chunk named by index.html (assets/index-DIaYPJCi.js): none of 'Stop running terminals', 'Switch to', 'Start the apps that were running last time', 'Quit Tinkerdeck', 'Update to', 'An app is a group of terminals', 'This removes the app and its terminals from Tinkerdeck', 'terminal(s) you removed are still running', 'Something may still be running in it', 'Switching branches changes the files' or 'Check for updates automatically' is in the initial chunk; they are all in CommandPalette-yFhYfqFV.js. The plan's section 7 claim that the initial view carries none of the dialog bodies is now true.)

findings.description: R1's pitfall forbids relying on source reading alone: the plan must be checked against the running app, including the real on-screen look and the CSS, before/with the window change. Do the running-app pass (or record what was actually observed on screen) instead of deferring it to a later merge gate.
findings.evidence: The plan's own §10 says it was 'Checked per screen against the component source and its CSS module, and against the existing Vitest suite that renders it. The real on-screen look comes from the CSS modules listed in the last column; the manual npm run tauri dev sign-off is the merge gate' (lines 202-204) and 'the manual running-app pass is the last gate before merge' (line 214), while the Signed off column claims 'Developer, this run' (lines 208-211). So the plan was validated against source, CSS files and unit tests, and the running-app inspection is explicitly deferred.
findings.note: confirmed by the whole Challenge after being built (docs/ui-tidy-up-plan.md:206-227 is now '10. Running-app verification (A2)': it records the built window bundle (the dist/ assets the Tauri window embeds) being rendered and driven at 1280x800 and 900x560, and gives an on-screen result per screen (four named top-bar groups and the Utilities contents, the collapsed git chip and its expand/collapse toggle, the separate editor view, Utilities > Help, the 900x560 layout, and Ctrl+B collapsing the sidebar), each with the CSS modules behind it. The old 'manual npm run tauri dev sign-off is the merge gate' and 'last gate before merge' wording is gone, and line 227 states no part of the check is left to a later manual pass. The eight screenshots the section refers to exist in scratch/developer/scenes (home-1280.png, home-900.png, appview-1280.png, appview-git-open-1280.png, editor-1280.png, help-1280.png, utilities-open-1280.png, home-ctrlb-1280.png); I opened home-1280.png and it shows the grouped Brand/Appearance/Create/Utilities bar, the Shell select, the theme control, the accent '+ App' and the 'v2.0.0' footer described for Home.)

findings.description: Merge BranchMenu into a single plan entry (noting its dialog role there) so the inventory is unique and a reviewer can trace it to exactly one entry.
findings.evidence: P9 (line 54) lists 'Branch menu popover (features/git/BranchMenu.tsx)' and D10 (line 82) lists the same component a second time as 'Switch branch popover (role="dialog" in BranchMenu.tsx)', with the note '(listed under P9 as well; it is a popover, not a modal)'. R1 acceptance #1 requires that each part appear in exactly one place.
findings.note: confirmed by the whole Challenge after being settled without a Build (BranchMenu now has exactly one inventory entry: P9 at docs/ui-tidy-up-plan.md:54 ('Branch menu popover ... features/git/BranchMenu.tsx ... a popover, not a modal'). The dialogs intro at lines 67-72 says the branch menu 'is inventoried once, with the panels at P9, and is not repeated here', and the D1-D9 table (lines 74-84) no longer contains a BranchMenu/BranchMenu.tsx row, so the duplicate D10 is gone. The R1 uniqueness test also passes (npm test: 392 tests, 42 files), scanning every inventory row for each *.tsx exactly once.)

findings.description: Add up/down/enter selection and keep focus inside the modal so the VS Code-style palette is efficient from the keyboard (USR-006 §2.1 keyboard navigation / §5.8 accessibility).
findings.evidence: Only Escape is handled (lines 30-39). The list items run only through onClick (line 70); there is no ArrowUp/ArrowDown/Enter handling, no active-item state and no focus containment for the aria-modal dialog. The palette is opened by Ctrl+Shift+P, so the primary flow is keyboard, yet running a command needs Tab-to-button or the mouse.

findings.description: Reset the tools state when the app/repository changes (e.g. key GitBar by app id, or an effect) if every app view should start collapsed.
findings.evidence: tools is seeded only once with useState(() => !(collapsible && defaultCollapsed)) (line 24), and App renders GitBar without a key (src/App.tsx:434-443). The component instance survives switching apps, so after expanding the git tools in one app, opening another repo-backed app shows them expanded, contradicting the plan's 'the app view starts from the collapsed chip' (docs/ui-tidy-up-plan.md:48).

findings.description: Assert the layout behaviour the test names (e.g. the header has flex-wrap and the groups keep min-width:0 in TopBar.module.css) rather than only the DOM parent.
findings.evidence: The test 'keeps every group in the header flow so a narrow window wraps instead of clipping them' only asserts that each group's parentElement is the header (lines 84-88); it never checks flex-wrap, min-width or that controls do not overlap/clip. R3's edge case 'The grouped top bar stays usable at the window sizes the app supports without controls overlapping or clipping' is therefore not actually verified.

findings.description: R5 acceptance 'Parts that are not shown are loaded when needed rather than up front, so the initial view does not carry them' has no test that can fail: the new code-splitting of GitDrawer/ConsoleNav/EditPane/ThemeFinder/CommandPalette is unproven, and the Help/Update dialogs are still in the initial chunk.
findings.evidence: React.lazy wraps ConsoleNav, EditPane, GitDrawer, ThemeFinder and CommandPalette (src/App.tsx:41-45), but no test asserts any of them is absent from the initial view: a search of src for lazy/Suspense/import( in *.test.ts(x) finds nothing. src/App.editor.test.tsx:76-85 only counts the pre-existing CodeSurface chunk, which was already lazy before this revision. Replacing every new lazy() with an eager import leaves all 388 tests green. The Help dialog (src/App.tsx:671) and UpdateDialog (src/App.tsx:654, through the eager UpdateUI import at line 16) also remain eagerly loaded, so 'lazy-load dialogs' is not met.
findings.note: src/App.tsx:40-49 now React.lazy-loads ConsoleNav, EditPane, GitDrawer, ThemeFinder, CommandPalette, UpdateBanner, UpdateDialog and the new HelpDialog; the Help/Update bodies are no longer in the initial chunk. src/App.test.tsx:54-82 installs vi.mock evaluation probes with an atImport flag and that flag is cleared only after `import { App }` (line 83). The new test at src/App.test.tsx:339-352 asserts `lazyLoad.loaded.filter((m) => m.atImport)` is empty, so any eager import of an on-demand module would make the factory run while atImport is true and fail the test. It then opens Help and asserts the CommandPalette/Help chunk is evaluated after import (atImport === false). Ran `npx vitest run src/App.test.tsx`: 19 tests pass.

findings.description: The plan puts the branch popover in both the panel (P9) and dialog (D10) inventories, and the R1 test cannot notice a part appearing more than once, so the 'exactly one place' acceptance is both unproven and currently false.
findings.evidence: D10 'Switch branch popover (role="dialog" in BranchMenu.tsx)' says it is 'listed under P9 as well'; P9 (line 54) describes the same BranchMenu popover. The plan therefore lists one part in two places, against acceptance 'each appears in exactly one place'. src/App.test.tsx:232-269 only does expect(plan).toContain(name), which cannot detect a duplicated entry.
findings.note: docs/ui-tidy-up-plan.md now inventories the branch popover once: P9 (line 54) is the only BranchMenu.tsx row, the D10 row is gone, the dialog table is D1-D9, and §3 (lines 69-71) states it is inventoried once with the panels. src/App.test.tsx:325-341 ('R1: the plan lists each part in exactly one inventory entry') parses every S/P/D/B/numbered inventory row and asserts each *.tsx basename appears in exactly one row; re-adding the old D10 row (which named BranchMenu.tsx) would make the count 2 and fail, so the acceptance is now proven rather than unproven. `npx vitest run src/App.test.tsx` 20/20 pass; full `npx vitest run` 390/390 pass; `npm run lint` clean.

findings.description: The R3 edge case 'the grouped top bar stays usable at the window sizes the app supports without controls overlapping or clipping' is asserted only structurally; the assertion cannot detect clipping. The wrap rules are present in the CSS, but the test does not prove them.
findings.evidence: The test 'keeps every group in the header flow so a narrow window wraps instead of clipping them' only asserts group.parentElement === header (line 87). It never checks flex-wrap or min-width, so removing 'flex-wrap: wrap' from TopBar.module.css (line 3) still passes.

findings.description: The R4 Ctrl+O conflict edge case is only half covered: the 'shortcut is not added' half is tested, the 'plan records the conflict and the chosen alternative' half is not.
findings.evidence: The test proves Ctrl+O is not matched ('not added'), but no test asserts the plan records the conflict and chosen alternative, which it does at docs/ui-tidy-up-plan.md:142-145.

findings.description: R5's edge cases 'a part needed while something happens elsewhere, such as console output arriving, stays reachable' and 'the plan says how many steps it takes and where the entry sits' are not covered by a test.
findings.evidence: The Console tab is only exercised in an app with no repository (T35, line 253) or with the git tools already expanded. No test asserts the Console stays reachable while the git tools are collapsed, and no test covers the 'how many steps to open a hidden part' edge case.
